variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Training data management is the discipline of turning raw observations into versioned, validated, documented, and governed datasets that can safely produce ML models. It covers where examples came from, how features and labels were created, which records entered each split, what quality checks passed, and who may use the result.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Start with three concrete objects”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Training example
pairs.detail: One entity or event represented by input features and, for supervised learning, a target label.
pairs.explanation: One entity or event represented by input features and, for supervised learning, a target label. It also needs identity, timestamps, provenance, and split assignment.

pairs.label: Dataset candidate
pairs.detail: A proposed collection of examples still being built, labeled, filtered, or validated.
pairs.explanation: A proposed collection of examples still being built, labeled, filtered, or validated. It must remain isolated from training jobs that require released evidence.

pairs.label: Dataset release
pairs.detail: A candidate promoted under a stable identity after required checks pass.
pairs.explanation: A candidate promoted under a stable identity after required checks pass. Corrections create a new release; they do not silently rewrite the old one.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is: every trained model must resolve to one immutable dataset manifest, and that manifest must resolve to exact source data, transformations, labels, splits, checks, and permissions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Training example: One entity or event represented by input features and, for supervised learning, a target label. Dataset candidate: A proposed collection of examples still being built, labeled, filtered, or validated. Dataset release: A candidate promoted under a stable identity after required checks pass.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Manage the lifecycle as a sequence of release decisions”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Register sources
pairs.detail: Record origin, owner, schema, event time, sampling method, allowed uses, retention, and how corrections or deletions are received.
pairs.explanation: Record origin, owner, schema, event time, sampling method, allowed uses, retention, and how corrections or deletions are received.

pairs.label: Build and label examples
pairs.explanation: Run versioned, point-in-time-safe transformations. Preserve label rubric, annotator or weak source, confidence, and adjudication.

pairs.label: Validate and freeze
pairs.detail: Check structure, distributions, duplicates, labels, slices, leakage, and policy.
pairs.explanation: Check structure, distributions, duplicates, labels, slices, leakage, and policy. Quarantine failures; sign a manifest only after gates pass.

pairs.label: Trace and maintain
pairs.detail: Link model runs to the release, monitor data behavior, investigate corrections, and propagate retention or removal actions through lineage.
pairs.explanation: Link model runs to the release, monitor data behavior, investigate corrections, and propagate retention or removal actions through lineage.

variants.prompt: Which statement best captures the core training-data-management invariant?
options: Every model must use the newest available rows
Every dataset must fit in one storage system
Every model must resolve to an immutable manifest that resolves all training evidence
Every training run must use the same algorithm
variants.explanation: The manifest connects a model to exact sources, transformations, labels, splits, checks, and permissions.
optionFeedback: The manifest connects a model to exact sources, transformations, labels, splits, checks, and permissions.
